Variants.Content: Dreadhole Castle is a castle on the coast of the royal territory. Its name retains the gloomy impression brought by the coastal terrain. Caves, steep slopes, woodlands or reefs along the coast often lead local residents to write natural dangers into place names; to strangers, these names may seem like threats, but to those familiar with the land, they are just signs of wind direction, fishing grounds and rain shelters. The area where Terror Cave Fort is located is connected to Blackwater Bay and the Narrow Sea Route, so it is possible to come into contact with merchant ships, and you will also hear news of smugglers, pirates and distant wars. Its fixed value is coastal observation and local control, and it should not be written off as an eternal outpost of one camp or another.

Entry Dyre Den If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

The craftsmen of Terror Cave Castle left behind their craftsmanship by using ship repair wood, canvas, salt, fish catch, and stones to resist the sea wind. The priests used the temples, flames and old dragon memories left when the Seven Gods and the Lord of Light coexisted to explain life and death. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Dyre Den They care about fishing, salt industry, wharves, volcanic rock fields and narrow sea shipping. They also care about whether seeds are left after harvesting grain and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
